title: Add hallucination prober and hit-rate quality gate
author: Diego Montes
description:
Motivation: regression monitoring today focuses on scalar metrics (accuracy, F1) and cohort drift, but we lack a lightweight, automated probe that detects subtle increases in hallucination rates for prompt-sets used by production routes. This PR adds a hallucination prober that runs in CI (and optionally as a scheduled backfill) and a hit-rate quality gate which fails CI when the fraction of outputs containing required factual anchors (hit-rate) degrades beyond a configurable tolerance compared to a rolling baseline.

What this PR does (summary): adds a new prober implementation (model-agnostic), an entailment-based lightweight verifier for anchor detection, a hit-rate gate that integrates with existing CI gate infrastructure, unit and integration tests, docs and runbook, and a small backfill worker to compute baselines for historical prompt-sets.

Key behaviors: - Sample-based prober: selects representative examples from a prompt-set (stratified by length and expected output type) and issues multiple perturbations (paraphrase + distractor injection) to stress hallucination modes. - Anchor extraction: prompt-set owners can declare one or more "anchors" (short canonical facts or ground-truth snippets). The prober checks presence and semantic entailment of anchors in model outputs rather than exact substring matches. - Hit-rate calculation: counts prompts where at least one anchor is validated, normalized over the probe sample. - Gate policy: compares current hit-rate to an exponential moving baseline and fails if the drop exceeds the configured absolute or relative threshold. Gate supports soft-fail (comment + label) and hard-fail (CI fail). - Backfill: a batch job to compute baseline hit-rates from historical runs and seed the baseline store for new prompt-sets.

Why this approach: purely lexical checks are brittle; entailment gives robustness and reduces false positives while remaining computationally lightweight compared to full human review. The gate is designed to be conservative by default (small tolerance, soft-fail) and to escalate only after repeatable regressions.

Checklist:
- [x] Prober implementation (eval_harness/probers/hallucination_prober.py)
- [x] Hit-rate gate (eval_harness/ci/gates/hit_rate_gate.py)
- [x] Unit tests and integration smoke (tests/probers/test_hallucination_prober.py, tests/ci/test_hit_rate_gate.py)
- [x] Backfill worker and baseline store adapter (tools/backfill/hit_rate_backfill.py)
- [x] Docs and runbook (docs/ci-gates/hit-rate.md)
- [x] Add CI hooks and GitHub action config snippet (ci/actions/hit_rate_gate.yml)

Backwards compat & config: the gate is opt-in for existing prompt-sets. New prompt-sets created via the prompt registry will default to a soft-fail policy and a 2% absolute tolerance relative to historical hit-rate. Ops can flip to hard-fail via project config.

Risks & mitigations: - False positives from noisy entailment: mitigated by threshold tuning, paraphrase ensemble, and a configurable minimum confidence. - Cost overhead: prober sample sizes are small (default 100) and entailment runs cache embeddings; backfill is rate-limited to off-peak windows.

Next steps: add Prometheus metrics (probe_latency_ms, hit_rate, gate_failures) and a dashboard to make regressions visible; add a Canary runner that runs the prober against a small live shadow traffic slice.

Notes on run: the initial runs were executed against three models (redwood/base-1, redwood/qa-2, open/llama-3) to validate behavior and to seed baselines for a subset of internal prompt-sets.

review_comments: Priya Shah: Good overall shape. Two asks: make the entailment confidence threshold configurable per-prompt-set, and add a test for paraphrase perturbations failing to flip anchors incorrectly.
Diego Montes (author): addressed config and added paraphrase test; moved default threshold to 0.82 and added comments on rationale.
Ethan Liu: Can we avoid calling the large entailment model for every sample? Suggest caching embedding for anchors and running a cheap cosine check as a pre-filter.

Diego Montes (author): added embedding prefilter and benchmark numbers in comments; cache TTL set to 12h and invalidated on anchor update. See eval_harness/utils/entailment_adapter.py for implementation.

Marcelina Gomez: integration tests look flaky on CI (intermittent network timeouts to the verifier). Recommend adding retry with exponential backoff and marking the gate runner as tolerant to transient verifier failures (soft-fail).
Diego Montes (author): added retries and circuit-breaker; updated gate to fall back to previous baseline on verifier outage and emit alert metric.
release_notes:
- Add hallucination prober: lightweight probe that validates presence of declared anchors via entailment-based checks.
- Add hit-rate CI gate: fails CI when validated anchor hit-rate drops beyond configured tolerance.
- Backfill job to seed historical baselines and adapter for baseline store.
- Opt-in by default (soft-fail) for existing prompt-sets; project-level config to enable hard-fail.
